"Scientists" do not always practice science.

In this article, Steven Novella presents an apparently high-minded discussion about a bill "that would change the way appointments are made to the science advisory panel of the EPA" by allowing those with closer ties to industry to fill positions.

Steven Novella does not mention that the bill is sponsored by a Republican, and gives scant attention to the type of bill it is -- deregulation. Though he fails to mention that the bill is Republican deregulation, he finds a convenient and rather colloquial quote from a Democrat who opposes the bill. He names the Democrat, Jim McGovern. He does not mention the sponsor, only the opponent. That's called a red herring, a straw man, and an attack. That's not called "science."

it is common for even academic experts to advise industry as well. I have seen trivial connections to industry used as a means of dismissing or discrediting relevant experts. We don’t want to scare academics away from providing useful advice to industry because doing so would forever taint their credentials or ability to serve on non-industry advisory panels.

He is okay with more industry influence, as he pretends that more industry influence is equivalent to more academic influence by claiming vaguely that industry and academia "commonly" work together.

It all depends on how such rules are enforced.

How are rules affecting industry being enforced in America today? Is this scientist expecting a miracle?

Boiling this down, Steven Novella is for more industry involvement in governance. Has he ever criticized too much industry in government? From what I've seen, he frequently criticizes government influence when it is an environmental or organic foods group. Those he seems to have no use for whatsoever. They aren't "science."

In his prior article, linked from this one, he claims that Greenpeace alone was able to get the EU to permanently end a "chief science adviser" because the current position holder was not anti-GMO. His own article contradicts this conclusion in so many ways you'd have to read it. He just needed to blame an environmental group for the ending of a controversial position. That's not science -- that's ideology.

Here is some fine advice:

What happens when your political or ideological views are contradicted by the consensus of scientific opinion regarding the evidence? It appears that a common reaction (depending on how strongly held the ideological views are) is to reject science. Not only do people reject the science specific to their issue, they reject science itself. They reason that if science disagrees with a view they strongly hold (and therefore “know” to be true) then science must be broken.

Those are the opening words of Steven Novella in that linked article. He needs to take his own advice. By the way, opening a science article with a paragraph like that is not scientific.Those things don't need to be said to the scientist, only to the masses. Just like the global warming deniers, he is going right around the scientific community and preaching to the public.In other words, his articles are propaganda.

Finally, I read through the comments and found this criticism of his ideology compelling.

This is a false equivalence: that academics and researchers (i.e., scientists) are beholden to ideological interests that are precisely equal to the interests of regulated industry. Do the math: assume everybody’s ideology cancels out everybody else’s. What’s left? Dollars and cents.

this is a matter of conflict of interest. At the very least it is asymmetrical to stack the deck such that some experts are excluded for fear they will act according to their own expertise, while advisors with monied ties to industry are allowed to specifically act in the interests of industry.

If only if only we could get people to protest our corrupt government instead of another issue that does nothing but to divide us. Still, I'm glad the american people are standing up for something.

A society is only as good as its most oppressed population. When you stand up against government violence upon this population, you not only help to unite the various sectors -- you also stand up for your own rights.

Found on Slashdot: Hacker Threatened with 44 Felony Charges Escapes With Misdemeanor

This is why people are protesting. This is why people are rioting.

Some states sign contracts with private prisons that require them to remain filled to a certain capacity. If enough crimes aren't committed, then the state just has to invent some.

Public defenders are overworked, underfunded, and more often than not are just prosecutors' assistants. They help prosecutors push "plea deals" used to bully people into guilty pleas without trial.

Some law enforcement agencies openly admit to having arrest quotas. The NYPD, for example, has been caught numerous times outright framing people for drug possession just to fill those quotas.

Civil forfeiture laws are abused by cops such that they fake probable cause, steal private citizens' property, never charge anybody with any crime, and if the citizens want their property back then the legal fight costs so much that they lose even if they win. And by the way, Obama's favorite to replace Holder has praised this policy of blatant thuggery and legalized robbery.

The worst civil forfeiture case I've heard of involved a couple who were told that the police would take their child away if they didn't turn over the cash in their glove compartment. However attorneys rationalize it, that is no different from having some street thug threaten to kidnap your child if you don't hand over your wallet.

Police violence steadily increases, and the underlying reasons are the lack of justice in this country rendering citizens more hostile, double standards in self defense laws, a total lack of accountability, and a general culture that says it's okay for cops to kill citizens. Any of us who are not law enforcement would have been expected to let Michael Brown beat us down.

The police do not serve people who do not have the funds to sue the city, county/parish, or state. If you don't have those kinds of teeth in the courts and you call them for help, you'll only get a lengthy, more polite, "Go fuck yourself, we don't care," out of them. They don't care what the law says. They don't enforce it. If you're a victim, you're better off moving than calling the police.

We live under drug laws engineered not to combat drug abuse but to fund police departments and create a class of people to dehumanize while those who treat humans like trash are praised for it. If you're poor and you deal with the courts then in most circumstances, it's drug test after drug test after drug test even if you are drug free and there's no reason to do that. Why? They say "procedure", "It's what we usually do." But why is it "procedure"? Because when somebody tests positive even for a light drug, everything about justice, equality, and the law goes out the window and the person who tests positive can be treated as subhuman without anybody questioning it.

I hope for these protests to be peaceful, but there is a part of me that is glad there are rioters because if things don't start to change then something has to happen to force that change. We can be arrested for nothing. We can be bullied into a guilty plea even if the accusation didn't even happen for anybody at all to be accused. We are not protected and we are not served. We exist outside the law, where it is not obeyed by officers in any way to benefit us but is abused incessantly to harm us.

I was threatened with arrest when somebody broke into my home and stole my belongings. When somebody renting a room brought firearms into my house that were supposed to be in storage, and implied that they'd shoot me if I tried to evict them, I was told it was a civil matter and threatened with arrest for calling the police. When a man admitted to showering with my daughter multiple times when she was four years old, the chief of police himself told me I would go to prison for reporting it. And then the investigation that did happen consisted of them asking her, now seven years old, if that happens now. Then they left her in his custody, and he's not even related to her, even though absolutely no abuse or neglect can be shown on my part or her mother's.

That's still in court. Oh, but guess who the law doesn't benefit when we can't spontaneously drop thousands upon thousands of dollars on an attorney. And therein lies the root of all this evil. Attorneys cost in the range of cars and cheap homes, and if you can't pull that kind of money out of your rear end on a moment's notice then you have no rights and the law does not protect you.

There is no justice in this country. When the law doesn't protect the poor unless they manage to pay it to, and the rich can literally get away with killing people, there is no law. There are only soldiers who detain, beat, and shoot us. They're not law enforcement because, again, in effect there is no law for them to enforce anymore. They're soldiers who keep the riff raff, the stinky poor, in line.

Obama is making this into a race issue. So, I guess that's a sign that we'll still be living in hell for a while. And we all know that means there will be more protests, more riots. I wonder what divisive distraction they'll blame the next one on. Since the frequency of the catalysts for these events keeps increasing, it follows that these events will become more frequent too. I wonder how often riots will have to happen before our government cuts the crap and addresses the actual problems.

This isn't about race because all of these things don't happen to black people but to poor people. It just happens that due to historical influences setting the stage, a higher proportion of black people are poor. This isn't a war by our government against black people, but it absolutely is a war against poor people. If you're poor, you have no rights, no safety, and to our government, you have no value.

I do not indict capitalism in saying this. I am not criticizing the rich. That's the first counterargument to come, and it's a distraction that intentionally misses the point. The problem isn't the rich. The problem isn't capitalism. The problem is that our government has treated justice like a business for so long that it has forgotten that justice is not capitalism; one is an economic system and the other is a vital institution without which civilizations end.

I don't like that businesses have burned. I certainly don't want anybody to get hurt. But the handful of livelihoods destroyed by rioters are a drop in the bucket compared with the millions upon millions of lives destroyed by lack of justice in this country, and we still are not having an honest conversation about it. So if it takes a few middle class gentry seeing what it's like to trigger the right discussion, let it be, regrettably. The people doing it are as stupid as they are brave, but God bless them because that type of mind has a purpose and place in society when things get this bad. God knows we've tried everything else short of waving a magical wand.

Although we'd pretty much be better off asking our fairy godmothers for deliverance than voting or petitioning the backward oligarchy, round-the-clock media tapdancing show, and flim-flam legislation market our government has become.

The one positive thing I can say is that where peaceful protesters are concerned, I've never seen such admirable and tolerant respect for Constitutional rights from our police before. Minding that I've only been politically active since the tail end of the Clinton era, I've seen "free speech zones," brutality against protesters, media slander and libel of protesters, and in this case all that they're doing is misdirection. It's an improvement, and the police who have shown restraint and patriotism deserve praise for that. Let's keep in mind that they're just the foot soldiers for the system, and that they'll serve a just and functional system just as passionately if ever the issues are corrected.

Buildings are buildings. They'll be rebuilt. Businesses will be rebuilt. Stuff can be replaced. I hope that even the rioters keep in mind that people can't be rebuilt. People can't be replaced. And I'm happy that with few incidences otherwise, even the most angry of the rioters have kept that in mind.
